articles.title: US and UK to host Women's World Cups in 2031 and 2035
articles.summary: FIFA has confirmed the United States, alongside Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica, will host the 2031 Women's World Cup — the first to feature 48 teams. The UK will stage the 2035 edition, its first…

image.caption: Spain are the defending champions going into Brazil in 2027Image: Frank Fife/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: FIFA have confirmed the hosts for the 2031 and 2035 Women's World Cup.

The United States, along with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica, was the only candidate to host in 2031, the first tournament that will feature 48 teams — as is the case with the men — for the first time. The US has hosted the tournamnent twice before, in 2003 and 1999, and is also the most successful country in World Cup history having won it four times.

After FIFA announced its revenue for the 2026 men's World Cup that finished just last summer was around $15 billionn (€13.7 billion), it is clear that US Soccer feels empowered that hosting the women's tournament is the next move forward. With the women's domestic league (NWSL) considered the strongest in the world and the US national team so strong, it is clear that securing the tournament in 2031 is a further sign of the US' committment to women's football.
"We expect and plan for the 2031 Women’s World Cup to be the largest women’s sporting event in history," Emily Cosler, US Soccer’s vice-president of strategy told The Guardian.
Two tournaments in seven years for the UK

The 2035 tournament was also awarded to the sole bidders, England, Scotland, Northern Ireland and Wales. This sees the World Cup return to the United Kingdom for the first time since 1966, the only time England's men's team won the competition. The women lost the 2023 final to Spain. It also means that the UK will host two major tournaments in relatively quick succession, with the men's 2028 European Championships also set to be held in England, Scotland and Wales and the Republic of Ireland.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the tournament would bring "visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country."

Given that FIFA President Gianni Infantino had revealed last year that both bids were unchallenged, this news comes as little surprise. Nevertheless, with the hosts now official, a 48-team tournament marks a remarkable growth for the women's game. For reference, the 2011 World Cup in Germany had just 16 teams.
The next World Cup will be in Brazil next year. Eighteen of the 32 teams have already secured qualification, including Germany, for the tournament, which runs from June 24 to July 25.

articles.title: Turkey: Authorities search for lioness on the loose in Istanbul
articles.summary: A lioness was on the loose in northern Istanbul, with wildlife advocates demanding answers over how the animal entered the country and who was keeping it in captivity.

image.caption: Prosecutors in Istanbul said an investigation was underway to establish who owned the animal [FILE: January 14, 2026]Image: Tokyo Zoological Park Society/REUTERS

blocks.text: Turkish security forces and wildlife authorities were searching woods in the north of Istanbul on Monday for an animal believed to be a lion that was reportedly roaming free, the national parks authority said.

In an online statement, the parks authority said police officers in the Zekeriyakoy area, north of Istanbul's European side, reported spotting "an animal resembling a lion" on surveillance cameras at around 9 p.m. (18:00 GMT) on Sunday.

Grainy images published by the Turkish media showed the lioness walking through a grassy area. It was unclear where the animal came from, though some media reports suggested it had escaped from a nearby home. The Istanbul Chief Public Prosecutor's Office said it launched investigation focused on identifying its owner.
Istanbul governor's office said in an online post, the location of the lion has been identified and the efforts to capture it were underway.

blocks.caption: Turkish media published thermal images of the lioness roaming freeImage: Anka

blocks.text: According to park authority, the search is still underway, with specialist veterinarians also involved in the operation to capture the animal.
Outcry among activists

Last year, a lion that escaped from a "theme park" near the southern city of Antalya was shot dead after attacking a man. It remains unclear where the Istanbul lion escaped from but it sparked an outrage among activists and advocates.
Northern Forests Defense, an independent ecology advocacy movement, called for "the individuals who illegally held this lion captive to be identified and brought to justice."
"Removing wild animals from their natural habitats and keeping them in captivity in villas is a crime," it said on X.
Wildlife conservationist Gokce Coskun said on X that "there are thousands of people keeping lions illegally in Turkey" and "licensed 'lion parks' have sprung up everywhere."

Doganay Tolunay, an ecology professor at Istanbul University, said questions must be raised about how a globally threatened species was brought into Turkey, how it passed through customs and why those keeping it have not been identified.
Although keeping wild animals as pets are forbidden in Turkey, it has become a hub for the illegal trade in wild animals as traffickers exploit its air links to Africa and Asia.
In December 2024, a young gorilla was rescued after being discovered at Istanbul Airport on a flight from Nigeria to Thailand.

articles.title: Leaked data shows more than 1,000 Russian military suicides during Ukraine war
articles.summary: Exclusive: Figures from cache of 11m death certificates reveal suicides account for about a regiment of Russia’s war dead
articles.byline: Pjotr Sauer, Michael Goodier and Harriet Agerholm

blocks.text: In late October 2024, Alexei Bolgov, a sergeant guarding a military headquarters in the occupied Donetsk region, told his wife, Natalya, over the phone: “It’s horrific, what’s going on here. I’ll tell you when I get back.”

He never made it home. Five weeks later, shortly after turning 29, Bolgov walked about 300 metres from his unit’s command post near the village of Stepove into woodland and shot himself, according to a written account by his commander seen by the Guardian.
“On the day of his death, Bolgov was in a withdrawn state,” his commander wrote.

Bolgov is one of more than 1,000 Russian soldiers recorded as having died by suicide since the start of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, according to confidential data from Russia’s state statistics agency, Rosstat, analysed by the Guardian.

The deaths of a further 885 soldiers in or near Ukraine were recorded as firearm-related injuries of “undetermined intent”, a classification that experts say can conceal suicides and that was used in several cases independently identified by the Guardian as suicides.
Taken together, the suicides amount to approximately a Russian regiment of dead.

The data, which analysts say almost certainly underestimates the true number of suicides, offers a rare, previously unreported glimpse of the strain on Russia’s armed forces nearly five years into a war in which heavy losses and harsh discipline have sapped morale.
Suicides among soldiers are a feature of most wars. A New York Times investigation found that at least 158 active-duty US army soldiers died by suicide in 2023.

But in Russia’s army, military analysts say, the problem is compounded by intense pressure from fellow soldiers and commanders, as well as fear of being sent on extremely dangerous combat missions. Contracts that in effect leave soldiers with no way out of the war add to the sense of desperation.

blocks.caption: Young Russian marines recruits attend a departure ceremony to join the army in St Petersburg in June 2024. Photograph: Anatoly Maltsev/EPA

blocks.text: “There’s clearly a lot of coercion used by the Russian military to force people to go forward. In some cases, they will abuse them, torture them, use different types of physical abuse,” said Rob Lee, a senior fellow at the Foreign Policy Research Institute. “So it’s not surprising that some guys commit suicide,” he added.
The figures come from a cache of more than 11m death certificates obtained by the Belarusian opposition-linked hacking group Cyber Partisans and the Ukrainian hacker collective Silent Crow.
The Kremlin does not publish data on suicides in the military and treats casualty figures as a state secret.

Of the 1,087 suicides by military personnel identified by the Guardian, at least 614 took place in occupied areas of Ukraine or Russian regions bordering it, mainly Belgorod and Bryansk. A further 113 records did not specify a location of death.
More than half of suicides involved firearms – particularly those near the frontlines. The deaths occurred at military camps, combat positions, training grounds and private homes.
Of those suicides that took place in the war zone, 43 were young soldiers aged 18 or 19.

The figures also include 108 men under 25 who died by suicide elsewhere in Russia away from the front. Some are likely to have been conscripts, who are not formally sent to fight in Ukraine but have often been pressed to sign contracts that allow them to be deployed.

blocks.caption: Russian conscripts attend military training at a ground training range in the Rostov-on-Don region, southern Russia, 21 October 2022.  Photograph: Arkady Budnitsky/EPA

blocks.text: Recorded military suicides have risen as the war has gone on, from more than 50 in 2022 to more than 200 in 2024, peaking at 365 in 2025 – mirroring Russia’s overall death toll. In 2026 – despite records being incomplete and lagging behind the battlefield reality – the database already records almost 300 suicides, the second highest total for any year of the war so far.
Activists and lawyers who work with Russian deserters believe the real number is higher.
“I would say it is a low estimate,” said Ivan Chuvilyaev, a spokesperson for Idite Lesom, a group that helps Russian soldiers desert. “Obviously, it is a lot more.”
He described the frontline as “a tin can” from which little information escapes. “Any Rosstat statistic, like any statistic relating to the war, is just reports passed up the chain.
“A man can kill himself, and on paper he is a hero. His parents might even be sent some medal,” Chuvilyaev said.
Officials, he added, had little interest in an accurate count, as the figures would be scrutinised further up the chain of command.
after newsletter promotion

Chuvilyaev and Lee also suggested that most cases in which Russian soldiers took their own lives on the battlefield, often after being wounded or as a Ukrainian drone approached, would probably be recorded as combat deaths rather than suicides. Such incidents have been documented in numerous grim videos from the front.
The gaps are visible in the Rosstat data.

Sergei Savenok, a 62-year-old lieutenant colonel from the Irkutsk region, volunteered in September 2022. Before leaving for the front, he is seen in a video clip taking to the stage of his local community centre to address the men heading off with him. “I’m from Donbas myself. Let’s fucking smash them, lads! That’s all!” he shouted, to applause.

He was found shot dead in occupied Luhansk region in July 2023. His wife, Yelena was informed by officials that his death was suicide, but he does not appear among the suicides in the Rosstat records.
A certificate matching his date of birth instead records a death from injury resulting from the discharge of a handheld firearm, with undetermined intent.
The Guardian was able to identify 1,038 military related deaths with similar causes – 885 of which took place in Ukraine or a bordering region of Russia.
Nor does Alexander Lazor, a 21-year-old private who died near the village of Solodke in Donetsk region in the summer of 2022, appear among the suicides in the records.

blocks.caption: Young Russian marine recruits sit in a bus during a departure ceremony to join the army in front of the Trinity Cathedral in St Petersburg, May 2023.  Photograph: Anatoly Maltsev/EPA

blocks.text: His family was told he was killed in combat, and in Rosstat data he is listed to have succumbed to “injuries due to warfare caused by firearms”.
But two soldiers who served alongside Lazor told the Guardian that members of their unit had been informed he had taken his own life.

“Our whole unit was told he killed himself. Perhaps, they decided to cover it up so that our unit doesn’t look bad,” said one of the soldiers, who spoke on condition of anonymity, speculating about why his comrade’s death had not been officially recorded as a suicide.
The suicides are just one sign of an army under strain.

By the end of May 2025, Russian military courts had received cases against 20,662 men for refusing to serve, most for going absent without leave, according to the independent outlet Mediazona. IStories verified this data and found at least 49,000 servicemen of the Russian armed forces had been declared deserters or Awol.

blocks.caption: A satellite image shows a view of new graves at the Starokrymske cemetery in Mariupol on 3 April 2022. Photograph: Maxar Technologies/Reuters

blocks.text: Thoughts of suicide were common among the soldiers Idite Lesom helped to desert, Chuvilyaev said.
“Of course they appear,” he said. “It’s the next stop, after a man realises where he has ended up.”

articles.title: Marcos, Liza take time off to recharge
articles.summary: After hurdling hectic schedules before and during the Association of Southeast Asian Nations and Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summits, President Marcos took two days off to recharge and bond…

blocks.text: November 24, 2026 | 12:00am
In her Facebook account, Liza uploaded a photo of her and the President in plain clothes spending some quiet time together in Baguio City.
Liza Marcos / Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — After hurdling hectic schedules before and during the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summits, President Marcos took two days off to recharge and bond with First Lady Liza Marcos.
“After a whirlwind of activities these past few weeks, we finally decided to take Sunday and Monday off to slow down, rest and recharge,” the First Lady said in a post published yesterday.
“No big plans, no fuss… just a little peace and quiet and some much-needed downtime together. And so far, we’re loving it!”
Marcos hosted the ASEAN Leaders Summit from Nov. 15 to 17 and welcomed US President Donald Trump at Malacañang on Nov. 18.
He flew to China to participate in the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders Meeting on the same day and returned to the Philippines last Friday.
Marcos previously said his participation at APEC – his 48th foreign trip since becoming President in 2022 – yielded “concrete” results for the Filipinos.
He said his business meetings in China generated P41.1 billion in investment pledges across various sectors that may create more than 7,000 jobs.

articles.title: Senate ethics body to tackle Bato’s ‘unsigned’ response
articles.summary: The Senate ethics committee will tackle Sen. Ronald dela Rosa’s unsigned response to the complaint against him for his absences, according to committee chairman Senate President Pro Tempore…

blocks.text: November 24, 2026 | 12:00am
Sen. Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa attends the Senate session on Monday, May 11, 2026, hours before being placed under Senate protective custody amid reports of an alleged ICC arrest warrant.
Senate PRIB

MANILA, Philippines — The Senate ethics committee will tackle Sen. Ronald dela Rosa’s unsigned response to the complaint against him for his absences, according to committee chairman Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente Sotto III.

Dela Rosa has asked the Senate body to “hold the complaint in abeyance,” pending his petition before the Supreme Court against the enforcement of the arrest warrant issued against him by the International Criminal Court for crimes against humanity.
Sotto yesterday said his office received on Saturday Dela Rosa’s answer to the ethics complaint filed by the group “Wag Kang KuCorrupt.”
But Dela Rosa’s answer did not carry his signature and was filed through his counsel, Sotto said.
“I received the answer via email on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026, 8:51 p.m. It was submitted through his counsel and not signed by him personally,” Sotto said.
“This answer will be considered in the next ethics hearing that will be scheduled at the soonest time,” he added.

In his answer posted on Facebook by his counsel Israelito Torreon, Dela Rosa said he “does not take lightly the duty of a senator to be present, nor the right of any citizen to ask this committee to hold a member to account.”
He said the complaint was only based on “templates, opinion and news” and is only “forcefully worded,” which “establishes no violation of any rule.”

“The Senate’s power to discipline its members is a serious constitutional power and an essential component of legislative independence. It must be exercised with restraint, on clearly defined standards and on concrete evidence,” Dela Rosa said.

The Senate ethics committee is also eyeing amending the Senate rules, which are silent on punishing absences. Dela Rosa has missed his Senate duties since November 2025, until he briefly surfaced last May 11 to help elect his ally Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano as a short-lived Senate president.

articles.title: Philippines extends 14-day visa-free privilege for Chinese nationals
articles.summary: The Philippines has extended the 14-day visa-free entry privilege for Chinese nationals for another year, from Jan. 16, 2027 until Jan. 15, 2028, the Department of Foreign Affairs announced yesterday.

blocks.text: November 24, 2026 | 12:00am

The DFA said the extension is in line with President Marcos’ directive to boost international tourist arrivals and investments in the Philippines, while maintaining existing immigration and national security safeguards.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines has extended the 14-day visa-free entry privilege for Chinese nationals for another year, from Jan. 16, 2027 until Jan. 15, 2028, the Department of Foreign Affairs announced yesterday.

“Under the arrangement, Chinese nationals may be granted visa-free entry for a stay not exceeding 14 days, exclusively for tourism or business purposes. The privilege remains non-extendible and non-convertible to any other Philippine visa category,” the DFA said.
Eligible travelers must possess a passport valid for at least six months beyond their intended stay, confirmed hotel accommodation or booking and a return or onward ticket.

The DFA explained that the extension remains subject to existing immigration and security safeguards, including the allowed entry of Chinese nationals availing themselves of the visa-free entry privilege through the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) in Metro Manila and Mactan-Cebu International Airport (MCIA) in Cebu only.
Travelers must comply with applicable eTravel registration requirements and have no derogatory records with the Bureau of Immigration (BI).

The admission into the Philippines, according to the DFA, remains subject to inspection, screening procedures and determination by the BI, including applicable identity verification, watchlist checks and risk-based assessment.
“The DFA will continue to coordinate with the BI and the law enforcement agencies on the monitoring of the implementation of the 14-day visa-free arrangement for Chinese nationals,” the DFA said.
The DFA also advised that Chinese nationals transiting through the Philippines and intending to enter the country en route to a third destination must obtain the appropriate Philippine transit visa.
The Department of Tourism welcomed the decision to extend the visa-free entry privilege of Chinese nationals until 2028.

According to DOT, Chinese arrivals to the country have increased by 70.18 percent and have reflected renewed visitor interest. Despite the brewing dispute in the West Philippine Sea, China remains one of the country’s largest source markets in 2026, ranking fourth at 6.87 percent. — Andrew Ronquillo

articles.title: DA: Adequate pork supply until Q1 2027
articles.summary: The Department of Agriculture has given assurance that domestic pork stocks remain adequate to meet demand until the first quarter of 2027 despite concerns that a 60-day import ban could lead to a…

blocks.text: November 24, 2026 | 12:00am
Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel Jr. said the country has enough locally produced and imported pork to meet consumer demand.
Andy Zapata Jr., file

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Agriculture (DA) has given assurance that domestic pork stocks remain adequate to meet demand until the first quarter of 2027 despite concerns that a 60-day import ban could lead to a supply shortage.

“The local industry stated that we have a lot of pork, and the data of the DA shows that we have a lot of local pork. We also have a lot of imported pork, so I think we won’t run out,” Tiu Laurel told reporters.
Earlier, a US Department of Agriculture (USDA) report warned of a potential pork shortage in the Philippines by the first quarter of 2027 due to the government’s two-month ban on imported pork.
The report noted that domestic production in the first three months of next year would have to increase by at least 14 percent to meet demand under a scenario involving reduced imports.
The Philippines consumed 430,000 metric tons of pork in carcass weight equivalent in the first quarter of 2026, according to the USDA.
The DA ordered a 60-day ban on pork imports after finding that surging foreign pork imports had caused serious injury to the country’s hog industry under Department Order 33.
The order is expected to take effect on Nov. 26.
Meanwhile, Tiu Laurel said meat processors had asked to be exempted from the import ban. He said he would meet with them on Nov. 24 to hear their concerns and assess their inventory.
“The processors have a request if they can be considered exempt from the 60-day ban. So, we’ll talk to the processors tomorrow to hear out. We’ll audit their stock levels,” he said.
Tiu Laurel added that representatives from the local hog industry would also attend the meeting, with the DA serving as mediator.

articles.title: Marcos gave ‘diplomatic’ response to Trump’s single-supplier proposal
articles.summary: President Marcos only gave a “diplomatic” response to US President Donald Trump’s suggestion that the Philippines source all its energy and agricultural imports from the United…

blocks.text: November 24, 2026 | 12:00am
US President Donald Trump (L) and Philippines' President Ferdinand Marcos Jr attend a luncheon at Malacanang Palace in Manila on Nov. 18, 2026.
AFP / Mandel Ngan

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos only gave a “diplomatic” response to US President Donald Trump’s suggestion that the Philippines source all its energy and agricultural imports from the United States, Philippine Ambassador to the US Jose Manuel Romualdez said.
In an interview with “Storycon” on One News yesterday, Romualdez denied that Marcos responded with “yes, sir” when Trump proposed a single-supplier trade arrangement for the Philippines.
“President Marcos said, ‘if it can be supplied from the United States, why not?’ That’s essentially the essence of the conversation,” Romualdez said.
The ambassador stressed that any commitment would depend on negotiations between the two longtime allies, including discussions on costs and the feasibility of the proposal.

“The commitments, of course, will have to come after we have a complete discussion on how we’re going to be able to achieve the proposal of President Trump,” he said. “But at the end of the day, it’s a trade deal, which means you say both parties have to look at the cost and how it would be able to get to that point.”
While recognizing the close relationship between the Philippines and the US, Romualdez said economic considerations would remain crucial in determining whether the proposal could be pursued.
“If it can be supported by the United States at a cheaper price, (then why not?),” Romualdez said.
“We’re open to the possibility. That’s (the message that) President Marcos sent… When you have a meeting like this, you don’t close the door and say, ‘no, we can’t do that,’” he added.

articles.title: VP defense struggling to find credible witnesses – prosecution
articles.summary: As the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte approaches its final stage, her defense team appears to be still struggling to get credible witnesses who can refute testimonies and…

blocks.text: November 24, 2026 | 12:00am
Impeachment court spokesperson Reginald Tongol yesterday announced the names of the witnesses who will testify during whole-day hearings from Nov. 9 to 13.
Senate SMU / Joseph Vidal

MANILA, Philippines — As the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte approaches its final stage, her defense team appears to be still struggling to get credible witnesses who can refute testimonies and documentary evidence presented by prosecutors, a spokesman for the House prosecution team said yesterday.

“They presented a supposedly expert witness, but his testimony was very far off from the Article of Impeachment that he had to rebut. Because if they really wanted to prove the VP’s innocence, they should have done that at the earliest by presenting their first witness,” Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong said at a news briefing.

He said it was evident that defense lawyers were unable to present witnesses who could directly shed light on the P817.87 million in alleged unexplained wealth of the Vice President and her spouse Manases Carpio.

“It speaks about how difficult it is for the defense really to look for witnesses that are competent, credible to provide documents before the court that will prove the innocence of the Vice President,” Adiong said.
His remarks came after the Senate impeachment court’s cancellation of the Nov. 26 and 27 hearings due to unavailability of defense witnesses.

The Lanao del Sur lawmaker said the primary issue was not whether the defense lawyers were being treated fairly, but whether they were prepared to present witnesses capable of explaining the evidence against Duterte.

“It’s about how prepared they are and how capable are they to really provide or present witnesses that can actually answer all these questions. And it’s really difficult for them,” Adiong, chairman of the House committee on suffrage and electoral reforms, pointed out.
It was forensic accounting expert Alexander Cabrera who earlier identified the P817.87 million in alleged unexplained wealth amassed by the Duterte couple from 2022 to 2025.
“The witnesses whom they decided to sit on the witness stand, they haven’t proven anything yet that could establish the VP’s innocence – even a single document,” he said.
He pointed out that the prosecution’s allegations were fully documented and supported by bank records, corporate filings, tax documents and Duterte’s statements of assets, liabilities and net worth.

Adiong and prosecution adviser and former congressman Robert Ace Barbers also said the Duterte camp may still rebut the withdrawn grave threat charges against the Vice President – but this time before the courts.
“They (defense lawyers) still have a venue. It’s not because the grave threats charges have been withdrawn in the Senate impeachment trial means they can no longer refute the charges,” Barbers said.
“So I really find it irrelevant to say that there is no more venue to answer these allegations in this article,” he maintained, adding the case is now with the Quezon City regional trial court.
Barbers was reacting to Duterte’s complaint about supposedly losing an opportunity to present evidence of alleged threats made by police personnel against her.

The grave threats against Duterte stemmed from her announcement at her online press briefing in November 2024 that she had contracted an assassin to kill President Marcos, First Lady Liza Marcos and former speaker Martin Romualdez.

In a statement last Saturday, Duterte claimed she had in her possession at least five documented threats allegedly made by police personnel against her, the Office of the Vice President and her family.
She blamed the prosecution’s withdrawal of the grave threats article for what she claimed was her lost opportunity to present the evidence at her Senate trial.
Barbers stressed the withdrawal did not end the separate criminal case against Duterte.

Philippine National Police chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr., meanwhile, has challenged Duterte to submit evidence supporting her allegations of police misconduct involving her former household staff member and four other people, saying such claims should be properly investigated.
He urged Duterte and her office to submit documents and other evidence that could help investigators establish what really happened. — Mark Ernest Villeza

articles.title: Gasoline down by P3 per liter, diesel by P2.60
articles.summary: Pump prices fall for the third consecutive week today, with gasoline down by P3 per liter, diesel by P2.60 per liter and kerosene, P1.60 per liter.

blocks.text: November 24, 2026 | 12:00am
Motorists queue at a gas station in Paco, Manila on Monday to refuel ahead of an expected fuel price rollback on April 14, 2026.
The Philippine STAR / Ryan Baldemor
MANILA, Philippines — Pump prices fall for the third consecutive week today, with gasoline down by P3 per liter, diesel by P2.60 per liter and kerosene, P1.60 per liter.
But the Department of Energy (DOE) does not expect the prices to go back to levels before the Middle East war anytime soon.

“I don’t want to be too positive because our readings show that it might not go back to that level,” Energy Secretary Sharon Garin told reporters yesterday when asked if the rollbacks would continue until Christmas.
Before the US-Iran war, gasoline, diesel and kerosene were sold for as low as P49, P48 and P77.40 per liter, respectively.
While international oil prices have eased amid improving supply conditions, Garin said the peso’s depreciation against the dollar continues to exert upward pressure on domestic pump prices.
Movements in foreign exchange rates are factored into the computation of weekly price adjustments.
Garin attributed the rollbacks to the recovery of oil exports from the Middle East, with more supplies from the region reaching global markets.
“Everybody has increased their exports, both OPEC (Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries) and non-OPEC producers. This means more supply is now reaching different countries,” she said.
The price cuts also reflect market sentiment following the US midterm elections, in which President Donald Trump’s Republican party suffered a crushing defeat.
The outcome eased fears of a further escalation in the Middle East war, which has been dragging on for nine months.
“The third reason is weak demand. Demand has declined. I think this is also a reaction to the increase in prices. When prices go up, demand goes down,” Garin said.
Gas stations
The number of allegedly erring gas stations that failed to comply with mandated price adjustments has doubled in a week, the DOE said.

Show-cause orders were served to 259 gas stations after field inspections showed they did not follow the exact amount of rollback set by the agency. That figure is up from the initial 114 flagged last week.
US import?
Meanwhile, if it would mean lower prices for Filipinos, the Philippines may “seriously consider” sourcing more of its oil and gas requirements from the United States, Garin noted.

This follows US President Donald Trump’s pronouncement, days after his bilateral meeting with President Marcos, that the Philippines had agreed to purchase all its agricultural and energy needs from the US.
Garin, however, clarified that negotiations between the two countries are still ongoing and that no final agreement has been reached yet.
“If it is cheaper, if the price is favorable and if it will help our fellow Filipinos, their offer is something to seriously consider,” she said at a media briefing.
Experts, meanwhile, cautioned against relying on a single supplier for the country’s fuel needs.

“Diversification of imported sources of oil/energy, agricultural products and other key imports would always be a prudent strategy, instead of concentrating the risks on just one or a few country sources,” Rizal Commercial Banking Corp. chief economist Michael Ricafort told The STAR. — EJ Macababbad

articles.title: COA chair hurdles CA confirmation
articles.summary: Commission on Audit Chairman Douglas Michael Mallillin received the nod of the Commission on Appointments yesterday despite an initial protest from one of the senators.

blocks.text: November 24, 2026 | 12:00am
Senators and Commission on Appointments officials have a group photo at the Senate yesterday with generals and flag officers of the Armed Forces of the Philippines.
Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — Commission on Audit (COA) Chairman Douglas Michael Mallillin received the nod of the Commission on Appointments (CA) yesterday despite an initial protest from one of the senators.

Before he received his confirmation from the CA committee and in plenary, President Marcos’ sister-turned-critic Sen. Imee Marcos grilled Mallillin about possible conflicts of interest in his work as the country’s auditor, noting his extensive experience with private firms.

She also flagged the COA’s role in helping the administration investigate the opposition, in an apparent reference to the disallowance of Vice President Sara Duterte’s confidential funds, an impeachment article that was later withdrawn by the House prosecution panel.
“Serious concerns have arisen over the manner by which the Commission on Audit has exercised its powers against members of the political opposition, both local and national,” Marcos said.

“I speak for many of these government officials, both elected and appointed, who are now worried that the COA, rather than serving exclusively as an impartial guardian of public funds, has been allowed to become an instrument of political harassment in certain cases, with its wide-ranging and considerable investigative and auditing powers being directed against those who dare to oppose the administration,” she added.
Asked to respond, Mallillin denied having any conflict of interest in his stint as COA commissioner before being appointed to replace Gamaliel Cordoba, who was named Supreme Court Associate Justice.
Mallillin’s term will only be until February 2029, serving Cordoba’s remaining term.
Mallillin vowed to “commit to be an independent commission as mandated by our Constitution without fear or favor” in response to Marcos’ claim of allowing the COA to be used for political harassment.

When asked by Sen. Risa Hontiveros what the COA intends to do with its confidential funds audit, Mallillin said the agency under his helm would “protect the identity of the people who are the informants and recipients of the funds, but without circumventing the internal controls that should be present in issuing confidential fund.”
Marcos later withdrew her opposition after colleagues put her protest to a vote, paving the way for Mallillin’s nomination to be approved and endorsed to plenary for final approval.

Sens. Joel Villanueva and Raffy Tulfo voted for Mallillin’s nomination in plenary, citing his experience as both lawyer and accountant and in having strict audit requirements, such as geotagging coordinates to prevent ghost projects.
Besides him, the CA confirmed the ad interim appointments and nominations of 15 generals and flag officers of the Armed Forces of the Philippines yesterday.
The CA also welcomed former Senate secretary Mark Llandro Mendoza as the CA’s new secretary.

articles.title: Forex exec in Romualdez case eyed as state witness
articles.summary: The Office of the Ombudsman has asked the Sandiganbayan to allow the removal of foreign exchange executive Felicito Guevarra from the list of accused in the plunder case against former House speaker…

blocks.text: November 24, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Office of the Ombudsman has asked the Sandiganbayan to allow the removal of foreign exchange executive Felicito Guevarra from the list of accused in the plunder case against former House speaker Martin Romualdez.

In an omnibus motion, ombudsman prosecutors also asked the Sandiganbayan Third Division to allow Guevarra to testify on the last hearing day on Dec. 4 on Romualdez’s petition for bail as well as to remain in the custody of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI). Plunder is a non-bailable offense.
The Sandiganbayan Third Division disclosed receiving the prosecutors’ motion at yesterday’s bail hearing.
Ombudsman prosecutors requested that Guevarra replace former Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) chief Manuel Bonoan as witness at the Dec. 4 bail hearing.
They also manifested their intention to withdraw their motion to have Guevarra’s passport canceled.

Aside from Guevarra, who is president of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corp., Romualdez’s co-accused are his former personal staff Joselyn Serenio and fugitive former congressman Zaldy Co. The case stemmed from Romualdez’s P7.4-billion alleged kickbacks from flood control projects.
After surrendering to the NBI over the weekend, Guevarra was given by the ombudsman conditional immunity from prosecution.

Deputy Special Prosecutor Omar Sagadal also revealed at yesterday’s hearing Guevarra’s restitution or returning of P343 million, representing his “share in his income from transactions with Romualdez through Serenio.”

Guevarra’s surrender to authorities, as well as his “willingness to come forward and divulge everything,” was “something we did not foresee and it happened so fast that is why we filed our motion,” according to Sagadal.

He added it would also be better to let Guevarra remain in NBI detention, instead of transferring him to the custody of the Bureau of Jail Management of Penology in view of allegations – already debunked – of visitors being let inside the New Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory to accompany Romualdez. Such setup would “put unnecessary risk” to Guevarra, the prosecutor said.
Sagadal also argued Guevarra substituting for Bonoan is compliant with current court rules. Bonoan will remain as a state witness, but not in the bail hearing.

“Our motion for amended information does not change the tune of the prosecution, does not change the allegation and maintains the conspiracy and plunder. All that is being done here is accused Guevarra be dropped as accused, but all are the same,” he said.
The camp of Romualdez through lawyer Rashel Ann Pomoy objected to the ombudsman’s proposal, arguing Guevarra’s supposed statement would be “prejudicial to the defense.”
She maintained that dropping Guevarra as accused “cannot be done through amendment of information” since Romualdez has pleaded not guilty to the plunder case.

Sandiganbayan Associate Justice Karl Miranda, chairman of the Third Division, said the bail hearings have been held “for 30 days” and were “extended” anew since the surrender of Guevarra. Yesterday was supposed to be the last day of the bail hearing.
Miranda also declared that the ombudsman’s motion involving Guevarra has been “submitted for resolution,” hence the uncertainty over whether he or Bonoan would be presented.
The court has scheduled for Nov. 27 the arraignment of Guevarra.

Prior to tackling the motion involving Guevarra, the prosecution presented lawyer Mark David Vergara, member of the ombudsman’s special panel of investigators that prepared the plunder case against Romualdez and the others.

According to Vergara, the ombudsman filed the P7.4-billion plunder case – lower than the P56 billion initially alleged against Romualdez and the others – based on sworn statements by 18 former security staff of Co who allegedly delivered cash in suitcases to three properties named under Romualdez’s alleged dummy companies.

Third Division justices, meanwhile, questioned how ombudsman investigators arrived at the alleged P7.4-billion amount linked to Romualdez, as a prosecution witness acknowledged that the figure was based on a computation of what the former security aides were able to recall.

Vergara, on questioning by the court, admitted that while the documents obtained by the investigation panel showed a bigger figure of P56 billion, the information only alleged P7.4 billion going by what the bodyguards of Co told them.
“I think the basis for the P7.4 billion was the testimonies of the Marines when they were able to make direct participation. It was just an estimate,” the witness said.

Vergara explained that the revised amount was based on specific alleged deliveries recalled by the former Marines, involving deliveries reportedly made two to three times weekly over approximately three years.

Pomoy, on cross-examination, got Vergara to acknowledge that he had no personal knowledge of the alleged suitcase deliveries beyond the statements provided by the former Marines, some of whom have already recanted their previous testimonies.
The investigator also confirmed that the characterization of the deliveries as being “for the benefit of accused Romualdez” was a conclusion reached by the ombudsman’s special panel of investigators.
The defense likewise quizzed the witness on how the panel gathered and evaluated the statements used to support the allegations.

Vergara conceded that the special panel of investigators did not personally interview certain individuals whose statements were included in the investigation, including former Marine Orly Guteza and Co.
“Guteza never appeared before the panel. We were looking for him but we did not get an address,” the witness said.
Affidavits from other witnesses, including Gil Navidad and Christopher Esquivel, had been executed before the special panel was constituted or were obtained through the NBI.
The cross-examination also brought up recantations executed by several individuals whose earlier statements had figured in the investigation.
Vergara confirmed that he was aware of recantations involving Guteza, Rosebert Waupan, Bernard Tube, Benny Boluntate and Cecilio Larroder.
The defense pointed out that Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla had previously expressed doubts about the statements from the former Marines and even called them “procured individuals.”

The defense also questioned the panel’s July 1 driving simulation involving Navidad, which was conducted to test the credibility of his account concerning locations where suitcases were allegedly delivered.
Vergara acknowledged that he did not participate in the simulation and had not checked whether Navidad’s phone could establish previous visits to the locations.
The questioning raised issues concerning the independent verification of witness accounts and the extent to which investigators corroborated the alleged deliveries.
Vergara, however, assured the court that the investigation was conducted with integrity and without bias.

articles.title: Senate begins plenary debates on budget bill
articles.summary: The Senate now girds for marathon floor debates on the P7.2-trillion national budget for next year, with its finance committee’s submission to the plenary of the chamber’s version of the…

blocks.text: November 24, 2026 | 12:00am
Senate finance committee chairman JV Ejercito said the Senate GAB has reverted “back to the basics” of funding food, health, education, employment and security.
Senate PRIB / Released

MANILA, Philippines — The Senate now girds for marathon floor debates on the P7.2-trillion national budget for next year, with its finance committee’s submission to the plenary of the chamber’s version of the 2027 General Appropriations Bill (GAB).
“Before we focus on complicated matters, we should focus what limited resources we have on ensuring that the basic needs of our people are provided,” Ejercito said.

The Senate allocated P378.6 billion for the Department of Health and its attached agencies and corporations, including P5.4 billion for the Health Facilities Enhancement Program for the construction and improvement of government hospitals and other health facilities.

The Senate also increased to P94.2 billion the government subsidy to the Philippine Health Insurance Corp. (PhilHealth), up from the House GAB version of P74.4 billion, to help realize the zero-balance billing program and reduce patients’ out of pocket expenses.

The Senate also reduced the P48.2-billion House allocation for the DOH program Medical Assistance Program, now rebranded from the previous Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP).
The Senate only allocated P16.2 billion for MAP, a P32-billion reduction from the amount in the House GAB version.
This will reduce the patients’ dependence on guarantee letters by allocating more funds for the universal health care program.
The Senate allocated P587 billion for the Department of Public Works and Highways for its various infrastructure projects next year.
To prevent a repeat of the flood control mess, Ejercito said the agency should prioritize completion of ongoing infrastructure projects and make sure the funds are put to good use.
The Senate also restored the P33.1-billion funding cut in the House GAB version on foreign-assisted big-ticket infrastructure projects.
This will help fund key infrastructure projects, such as the Bataan-Cavite Interlink Bridge, Laguna Lakeshore Road Network and Pasig Marikina River Channel Improvement Project, Ejercito said.

The Senate also restored the P4.7-billion government counterpart funding for foreign assisted projects, as well as the P15-billion loan proceeds each for the continued construction of the Metro Manila Subway Project and the North-South Commuter Railway.

To address the super El Niño phenomenon, the Senate earmarked P251 billion for the Department of Agriculture to help farmers with their crops, including P4 billion for its rice program and a P1-billion augmentation for the DA contingency funds.
As a response to the West Philippine Sea issue, the Senate gave the Department of National Defense an additional P1.73 billion in funding for a total of P326.9 billion.
This would be on top of the earmarked P50 billion for the Armed Forces of the Philippines modernization, Ejercito said.
The Philippine Coast Guard in the Senate version was allocated P45.6 billion, up by P146.8 million, to support its operations and maritime security efforts.
“The presence of our Navy and Coast Guard brings confidence to our fishermen who only wish to peacefully earn an honest living in the West Philippine Sea – without threat or intimidation.”

Meanwhile, the the League of Provinces of the Philippines (LPP) has welcomed the Department of Budget and Management (DBM)’s move to allow a case-by-case review of local governments’ performance in qualifying for 2026 Collective Negotiation Agreement (CNA) incentives.

The agreement followed a Nov. 19 meeting between Budget Secretary Kim Robert de Leon and representatives of the country’s local government leagues headed by LPP national chairman Isabela Gov. Rodito Albano, who cited procurement delays, failed biddings and calamities that have slowed projects meant to deliver infrastructure and basic services to residents. — Artemio Dumlao

articles.title: The rise and fall and rise again of Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Days after resigning while mired in scandal of extra-marital affairs, Nvidia's Jensen Huang is making a remarkable return.
articles.byline: Michael Race, Peter Hoskins, Lucy Hooker

blocks.text: It's being called a comeback for the ages.
For a long time it seemed that Jensen Huang, the leather jacket-clad founder of Nvidia, dubbed the "Taylor Swift of tech", could do no wrong.
Then came allegations of two affairs - one with a businesswoman suspected of being a Chinese spy - that rocked the world of tech and the global stock market. Huang resigned.
Now, just 11 days later, he's been reinstated by the board, who says it believes he is the right person to lead the company.
So what do we know about the man who is once again at the head of Nvidia, a linchpin in the US's race for technology leadership with China?
Huang may not be a household name on the same level as Elon Musk or Mark Zuckerberg.

But his role in the tech industry, especially in relation to the explosion of artificial intelligence in the last three years, may prove more consequential. Nvidia dominates the market for the microchips that are used to power the new technology.
The company is at the centre of the AI race between the US and China, the world's tech and economic powerhouses.
Huang enjoyed access to the seats of political power on an unrivalled scale, being courted by both US President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping.

His remarkable rise to the top of his profession saw him amass an estimated fortune of close to $200bn earlier this year, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, though that has since dropped to around $105bn.

Despite always donning his trademark all-black outfits and taking a playful approach to investor presentations, Huang has worked for years to present himself as a family man, someone who exemplified the American Dream.

Born in Taiwan in 1963, Huang and his family moved to the west coast of the US when he was nine years old. He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a Master's degree in the same field from Stanford University.
It was at college where he met his wife, Lori Mills. The pair were lab partners and married in 1985, eight years before Huang founded Nvidia.
They have two children, Madison and Spencer, who now both work in senior roles at Nvidia.

The company became a key provider of the computer chips and circuits used for gaming before it expanded in a new direction. It now creates the key processing chips used to power the growing AI technology.

Huang has hailed AI as a "new industrial revolution" that is on a par with the advent of electricity. Nvidia is the world's second most valuable company and its customers include the biggest firms on the planet, Google, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, SpaceX, Tesla, OpenAI and Anthropic, all spending big on its products.

So it is no surprise that at a recent AI summit at the White House, Huang was picked out from a group of 42 to flank the president, alongside Elon Musk, both men with whom Trump has famously close relationships.

"Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine, a biography on Jensen Huang, told the BBC, referring to the late boss of Apple. He added that Huang was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today.
He described him as a "demanding" boss, who "really pushes his people to the limit".
But while Huang is "very brilliant" and a "world-class computer scientist", there's also "a level of arrogance" and "a level of self-deception as well", he said.
Huang had gone to great lengths to present himself as a family man, he added, something that was "very important to him".

First reports emerged on 29 October in the New York Times that Huang had conducted a relationship with Alice Huang, no relation. US officials allege the businesswoman associated with Singapore-based firm Megaspeed is a Chinese intelligence asset.
Huang admitted to having been unfaithful to his wife and apologised for hurting their family.

But the reporting of a second affair, with Kimberly Powell, vice president of healthcare who has worked at Nvidia for 18 years, prompted a board meeting, followed by an announcement that Huang was stepping down.
He'd barely been gone, however, before a "Bring Jensen Back" campaign was launched, reportedly by current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and supporters.
The man himself said he would be "honoured" to return, should the board ask him.
Although initially showing no interest in reinstating him, the board has now done just that, saying his return was "in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers".

articles.title: Gukesh to defend chess crown against rising star Sindarov
articles.summary: As the World Chess championship gets underway, it's no coincidence that the titleholder, Gukesh Dommaraju, and his challenger, Jakhovir Sindarov, are both from Asia.

image.caption: Although he is the challenger, Javokhir Sindarov may be the favorite to beat title holder Gukesh Dommaraju Image: Salvatore Di Nolfi/KEYSTONE/picture alliance

blocks.text: When India's world chess champion, Dommaraju Gukesh, faced reporters at the pre-tournament press conference in Geneva on Sunday, there was no sign of the youthful, carefree energy one might expect from a 20-year-old.
"I don't think I'm here to defend anything—I'm here to win it all over again," he said.
Starting November 24, Gukesh will be facing challenger Jakhovir Sindarov of Uzbekistan for a purse of $2.5 million (€2.3m) in the World Chess Championship.

Gukesh captured the title in 2024, making him the youngest-ever world champion at just 18. Since then, however, things have not as gone well for the player known for his exceptional calculation skills and a penchant for risky moves. He currently languishes in 26th place in the FIDE world rankings.
The challenger as the favorite
Sindarov, who has climbed to number four in the world, told reporters that he only began training "seriously" last year and has learned a lot from observing the reigning world champion.
"He has a very good strength in typical positions, his calculation is very good, and Gukesh can fight until the end," Sindarov said.
Former world champion Viswanathan Anand, who was also one of the world's best players as a teenager, is not completely surprised by Gukesh's lack of form over the past two years.
"He became the world champion (very young). So suddenly the responsibility is shifted onto you and even expectations," Anand told DW.
"Clearly he has deficiencies in his chess as is normal for someone who's 20, he's not had time to experience a lot."
By the time he became India's first world champion, Anand was 37 – ancient by the age-standards of today's top players.
The computer generation
"With powerful chess software and global connectivity, it is easier for young players today to reach the top level," Jan Gustafsson, coach of Germany's national chess team, told DW.
"Online chess provides many more learning opportunities for talented players," added Gustafsson, who sees the recent movement at the top of the rankings as a "generational shift."

blocks.caption: Former world champion Magnus Carlsen now rarely competes in classical chessImage: Carina Johansen/NTB/IMAGO

blocks.text: While Norway's Magnus Carlsen, long considered the greatest player of all time, remains number one in the world rankings, he rarely plays classical chess anymore and gave up his world championship title after declining to defend it in 2023.

Now, young players—particularly from Asia—are pushing to the forefront. Alongside Gukesh and Sindarov, players such as Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa from India and Nodirbek Abdusattorov of Uzbekistan—an emerging chess powerhouse—are considered contenders to win a world championship in the not-too-distant future.
"Broad social acceptance and state support ensure that children can focus on chess at a very early stage," Gustafsson said.

Another contender is Germany's Vincent Keymer, who at 22 is number nine in the world and well established among the world's elite. Most recently, Keymer and his teammates won a bronze medal at the World Team Championship, often referred to as the "Chess Olympiad."
Additional reporting by: Thomas Lemmer

articles.title: London, Ont., police solve 1968 murder of teenager Jackie Dunleavy using genetic genealogy
articles.summary: London, Ont., police have solved a cold case involving the murder of teenager Jackie Dunleavy, who was found strangled in 1968 just blocks from where she went missing after a work shift at a…

image.caption: Jackie Dunleavy was 16 when she was killed in January 1968. Police in London, Ont., just announced they have solved her murder, using forensic genealogy. (Supplied by London Police Service)

blocks.text: London

London, Ont., police have solved a cold case involving the murder of teenager Jackie Dunleavy, who was found strangled in 1968 just blocks from where she went missing after a work shift at a convenience store.
16-year-old killed blocks from where she went missing, man found to be her killer died in 2018

Police used modern forensic DNA technology and genetic genealogy to identify Dunleavy's killer as Michael Joseph Moore, who was 25 at the time of the murder. He later became a firefighter in London, retiring with the rank of captain, police said.
Moore died on March 3, 2018, so no criminal charges can be laid, investigators said. At the time of the killing and in subsequent years, he wasn't a suspect or person of interest.
“This outcome reflects the extraordinary dedication and persistence of the investigators who worked on Jackie’s case, both past and present,” London police Chief Thai Truong said.

“Their professionalism, the careful preservation of evidence and advances in forensic science ultimately brought us to where we are today, providing long-awaited answers about who was responsible for Jackie’s death.”

Police announced the breakthrough at a news conference at their headquarters on Monday. Dunleavy's case is one of nine cold cases that they have been working on. Dunleavy's younger brother and his wife were at the announcement, but declined interviews.
Police said there's no evidence that Dunleavy and Moore knew each other.

Moore was born in Ireland in 1942 and emigrated to Canada in January 1967, police said. He moved into an apartment on Springbank Drive in May 1967. He was white, around six feet tall, had dark hair and was typically clean shaven, growing a beard sometimes while on vacation.

An obituary in the London Free Press states that Moore was a firefighter for 28 years, both in Ireland and London. He was not a firefighter at the time of the killing, police said. He died after a long illness and was survived by his wife and three children, it said.
The front page of the Jan. 10, 1968, London Evening Free Press highlights the Dunleavy case. (Supplied by London Public Library)
Dunleavy was a Grade 10 student at Westminster Secondary School and worked at Stanley Variety Store on Stanley Street, near Wharncliffe Road.
She was the daughter of a London police officer.

On Jan. 9, 1968, Dunleavy finished her shift at the convenience store at about 6:30 p.m. and was last seen walking away from the store, likely to catch a bus home, which she often did, reports said. Witnesses later said they remembered a girl fitting Dunleavy's description waiting at a bus stop on Beaconsfield Avenue and getting into a white vehicle. Moore drove a white Ford Galaxie 500.
These photos of Michael James Moore were released by London police. (Supplied by London Police Service)

At about 8 p.m. that evening, three young people found her remains on the grounds of Katherine Harley School, which is now the location of Matthews Hall, on Oxford Street near Sanatorium Road, in the city's west end.
Collecting biological material crucial

The cause of death was strangulation. News reports at the time revealed Dunleavy had a pink tissue box stuffed in her mouth. Investigators interviewed witnesses and collected biological material, which was preserved, police said.

“The investigators who worked on Jackie’s homicide in 1968 did everything they could with the investigative and forensic tools available to them at the time,” said Det. Sgt. Micah Bourdeau of the London police major crime section.

“The evidence they carefully collected and preserved ultimately allowed investigators decades later to continue that work. This investigation shows the importance of preserving evidence and continuing to revisit historical cases as new technology becomes available.”

Dunleavy's murder was recounted in the popular book The Forest City Serial Killer by local author and sleuth Vanessa Brown, as well as Murder City: The Untold Story of Canada's Serial Killer Capital, 1959-1984, by former London police officer Mike Arntfield.

Her case was part of Project Angel, a join London police and Ontario Provincial Police cold-case task force from 1997 to 2001. Moore's name came up during that investigation, which re-examined old murders, but he was not named as a suspect then and records have since been lost, Bourdeau said.

Investigators analyzed preserved evidence and sent DNA to Othram Labs, a Texas-based company that specializes in forensic genealogy, which combines DNA and genealogical databases to identify suspects, police said.

"DNA evidence and genealogical work narrowed the focus of the investigation," police said. "This led to further interviews and the collection of new forensic evidence. This evidence was compared to the suspect profile, confirming Michael Moore's DNA as the suspect profile."
Had Moore been alive today, he would have been arrested and charged in relation to Jackie’s murder.Det. Mike Budzyn, London police
Toronto police helped with the genealogical research, investigators said.

“The evidence established a level of certainty that would have supported criminal charges," said London police Det. Mike Budzyn. "Had Moore been alive today, he would have been arrested and charged in relation to Jackie’s murder.”
The decision to identify Moore was not made lightly, officers said.
"Publicly identifying Moore provides an accurate historical record and answers that Jackie’s family and the community have sought for decades," they said.

"Hearing the name Michael Joseph Moore, or learning information about him today, may bring back memories for people who knew him, had contact with him, or were familiar with him during that time. Information that may not have seemed significant at the time could have meaning today."
Anyone with information related to this investigation, or who believes they may have relevant historical information, is encouraged to contact the London Police Service at 519-661-5670.

articles.title: Prominent Zimbabwean preacher arrested on sexual assault allegations
articles.summary: Uebert Angel, a British-Zimbabwean national, leads a charismatic church with branches in several countries.

blocks.text: A well-known Zimbabwean preacher has been arrested on indecent assault and sodomy allegations, local police said.

Uebert Angel, who leads an international charismatic church with branches around the world, was arrested during a church service in Harare on Sunday. Pictures and footage of the dramatic arrest have since been circulated online.
In one video, a convoy of vehicles is seen escorting the self-styled prophet as he sits in the back of a police van surrounded by armed police officers.
The controversial founder of Spirit Embassy was also appointed Zimbabwe's special presidential envoy and ambassador-at-large to Europe and the Americas back in 2021 by President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

In 2023, he made headlines when an undercover report by Al Jazeera claimed that he had offered to use his diplomatic status to launder large amounts of money through a gold-smuggling scheme in the country.
According to the Qatar-based network, Angel, 48, told reporters working undercover that the scheme was approved by President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

Zimbabwean police only released a brief statement confirming his arrest but a member of his team told reporters the British Zimbabwean national was still in police custody and it was unclear when he'd make an appearance in court.

"It can be in the afternoon or tomorrow [Tuesday]. We are still within the legal framework [for him to appear in court]," Professor Lovemore Madhuku told state-owned broadcaster ZBC in a clip posted online.
This is not the first time the prominent preacher has been accused of improper behaviour.

A report by local online publication ZimLIVE in 2021 said that Angel had previously faced allegations of sexual impropriety from several women, at least five of whom are in England. The charismatic preacher has denied the allegations, the outlet added at the time.
Angel's church has branches in Zimbabwe, South Africa and the UK and he known for his ties to other African preachers like Malawian televangelist Shepherd Bushiri.

articles.title: Nepal's new PM eyes closer ties with India amid lingering disputes
articles.summary: On his first foreign bilateral visit, rapper-turned-Prime Minister Balendra Shah sought deeper ties with Nepal's neighbor and largest trading partner, while steering clear of sticky territorial…

image.caption: Shah's visit aims to reset ties that have been strained by tensions and disputesImage: Arun Sankar/AFP

blocks.text: For years, Nepal's relationship with India was shaped by familiar faces, as leaders of the Himalayan country's erstwhile three major parties took turns in the prime minister's office through revolving coalition governments.
This week's state visit to India by Balendra Shah, a 36-year-old rapper-turned-politician, marked a clear break from that pattern.
As a young, first-time prime minister with a strong electoral mandate , Shah represents a new political force in Kathmandu.

But long-standing economic strain, along with August's devastating flash floods and the Nepalese public's high hopes for more jobs, investment and better governance at home, have made Shah's first bilateral visit abroad more than a mere diplomatic box-ticking exercise.

To safeguard Nepal's flood recovery and development, Shah needs to get off on the right foot with his country's southern neighbor and largest trading partner and its long-standing prime minister, Narendra Modi.

While Nepal and India share an open border, as well as deep cultural and historical ties, their relationship has also been marked by territorial disputes and a desire in Nepal to be seen as an equal by its much larger and more powerful neighbor.
Constantino Xavier, a senior fellow at the Center for Social and Economic Progress in New Delhi, however, cautioned against expecting too much from a single visit.

"We need a big, long-term ambition coupled with small, short-term steps," he told DW, arguing that economic cooperation should remain the central focus of relations because it directly contributes to the socioeconomic development of both countries.
Economic cooperation takes center stage

The young prime minister's test is to turn a strong domestic electoral mandate and political goodwill with New Delhi into tangible economic gain, as well as to address longstanding border disputes and a massive trade imbalance.
Shah's administration sees diplomacy as key to addressing the country's development aspirations, which was reflected in bilateral talks with Modi on Monday.
Economic cooperation featured prominently during the talks as both sides sought engagements in trade, investment, connectivity and infrastructure development.

Kathmandu's priority was securing Indian financial support for reconstruction following the August disaster that claimed the lives of more than 1,450 people, while 5,745 are missing or unaccounted for.
The floods swept away roads, bridges, hydropower projects and settlements, with reconstruction bills estimated at around $4.8 billion (about €4.4 bln)

At a joint press briefing after their talks in New Delhi, Modi announced a package of $1.63 billion to help rebuild flood-hit areas and upgrade other infrastructure projects — around $380 million as a grant, with the rest as a concessional loan.

The South Asian neighbors also agreed to deepen cooperation across a wide range of areas, including trade, investment, connectivity and people-to-people ties, and launched a new long-term vision aimed at strengthening economic integration and development.

The talks also yielded commitments to broaden educational and innovation partnerships, boost energy and infrastructure cooperation, improve market access and trade links, and enhance landlocked Nepal's connectivity through additional air and port access via India.
Bilateral trust and unresolved differences

Shah's visit offered an opportunity to break the ice in a high-level exchange visit and improve a relationship periodically strained by political mistrust, territorial disputes and differing strategic interests.
Nepal and India both have competing territorial claims over Kalapani, Lipulekh and Limpiyadhura, a strategic Himalayan territory in northwestern Nepal.

As mayor of Kathmandu, Shah raised the border disputes with India, which helped boost his nationalist image and set his broader political agenda. However, his India visit steered clear of such contentious issues.
Why Nepal's elections matter to India and China
Bimala Rai Paudyal, a former Foreign Minister of Nepal, said Shah avoided tricky bilateral issues to focus on his administration's economic agenda.

"This visit could be a good starting point towards resolving the border issues that have been the key strain in our relations," she told DW. "But the new government didn't show interest or the guts to address this."
Yet, economic pragmatism should not mean indefinitely sidelining political differences.

Ashok Swain, head of the Department of Peace and Conflict Research at Sweden's Uppsala University, said the visit's success should be measured by whether the two countries can establish a predictable and mutually beneficial relationship.
"Nepal's territorial disputes, concerns over the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship and its economic and transit dependence on India need to be addressed," Swain told DW.

"Shah's biggest opportunity is to transform Nepal's geographical location between India and China from a strategic vulnerability into an economic and diplomatic asset," he added, arguing that Nepal should not be forced to choose between its two neighbors.

Whether the visit marks a tangible reset on the economic front will ultimately depend not on the number of agreements announced, but on how they are implemented and whether the two governments are willing to address the disputes that have long strained ties.

articles.title: DSWD suspends AICS guarantee letter release starting Nov. 30; cash aid still available
articles.summary: The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) will temporarily suspend the issuance of guarantee letters (GLs) under its Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situation (AICS) program…

blocks.text: Published November 23, 2026 10:44pm

The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) will temporarily suspend the issuance of guarantee letters (GLs) under its Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situation (AICS) program starting Nov. 30, 2026 to facilitate its annual liquidation process and settle outstanding payments to service providers.

DSWD spokesperson Assistant Secretary Irene Dumlao announced the temporary suspension on Monday, Nov. 23, clarifying that the measure will only cover guarantee letters and will not affect the distribution of outright cash assistance under the AICS program.

“Atin po munang pansamantalang ititigil ang pag-issue ng guarantee letters sa ating AICS upang mabigyan ng panahon ang Departamento na makumpleto ang taunang proseso ng liquidation at mabayaran ang mga obligasyon nito sa mga service provider,” Dumlao said.
“Kinakailangan po natin ito para masigurado na tuloy-tuloy ang serbisyo sa susunod na taon,” she added.

Dumlao assured the public that individuals and families experiencing crisis situations may continue to seek immediate financial assistance through the DSWD's Field Offices and satellite offices nationwide.

“Hindi po kinakailangang mangamba ang ating mga kababayan na nakararanas ng krisis dahil hindi po titigil ang outright cash ng AICS. Patuloy po kaming tatanggap ng kliyente sa aming mga Field Offices at satellite offices,” she said.
The issuance of guarantee letters is expected to resume on the first official working day of January 2027.
The DSWD urged the public to take note of the temporary suspension and monitor its official communication channels for further announcements. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.summary: The company's move to bring Huang back marks a sharp reversal from its board's decision just days earlier to rule out his return

blocks.text: JENSEN HUANG. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang arrives for a meeting with SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won at SK group’s office building in Seoul, South Korea, June 8, 2026.
Kim Hong-Ji/Reuters
The company's move to bring Huang back marks a sharp reversal from its board's decision just days earlier to rule out his return
Nvidia on Monday, November 23, said it is reinstating Jensen Huang as chief executive, effective immediately.
Nvidia shares surged on the news, jumping more than 25% in premarket trading.
The company’s move to bring Huang back marks a sharp reversal from its board’s decision just days earlier to rule out his return.

Huang built Nvidia from a video-game chip designer into the dominant supplier of AI processors, steering its chip roadmap, customer deals and Washington ties along the way. (TIMELINE: Jensen Huang’s fall from Nvidia grace)
He resigned on November 12 after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a businesswoman US authorities suspect of spying for China, an allegation Beijing denies.
The board said it was satisfied with Huang’s candor and leadership ability and, after receiving input from senior US government officials, saw no national security risk in his return. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Cayetano wants to let ‘generous’ Filipinos cover gov’t debt. Any takers?
articles.summary: 'If I want to be a good citizen and pay my share, P170,000, where do I go?' Cayetano asks, apparently keen to 'go beyond' paying his taxes to help settle the national debt

blocks.text: ALAN CAYETANO. Senator Alan Peter Cayetano gestures during a press conference concerning Senator Ronald 'Bato' dela Rosa, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court and who has reportedly fled, a day after gunfire rang out at the Senate, on May 14, 2026.
Noel Celis/Reuters
'If I want to be a good citizen and pay my share, P170,000, where do I go?' Cayetano asks, apparently keen to 'go beyond' paying his taxes to help settle the national debt

items: Senator Alan Peter Cayetano proposes a mechanism for individual taxpayers to contribute their share of the national debt, calculated at over P170,000 per Filipino.

During Senate discussions, Cayetano expressed his desire to pay this amount directly, highlighting a historical example from South Korea's 1997 financial crisis where citizens contributed gold to help their country.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
Senator Alan Peter Cayetano is concerned about the national debt.
So concerned, in fact, that he wants the government to set up a mechanism so that even you — yes, you, individual taxpayer — can directly pay your share of more than P170,000.

That’s P170,598.03, to be exact, which Cayetano calculated as each Filipino’s share of the country’s enormous debt. It’s not money you owe or any citizen personally owes the government, of course, but if you’re feeling particularly generous, the senator thinks you should have a way to chip in. Are you game?
During Senate deliberations on the proposed 2027 budget, Cayetano asked economic officials where exactly he could hand over his contribution.
“If I want to be a good citizen and I want to pay my share, P170,000, where do I go?” he asked.

blocks.caption: Cayetano wants to let ‘generous’ Filipinos cover gov’t debt. Any takers?

blocks.text: For a moment, Senator JV Ejercito, who chairs the Senate finance committee, seemed perplexed. He grinned, turned to the economic team for help, and suggested that perhaps the best contribution Filipinos could make was simply to pay the right taxes.
“That’s not true because I’m already paying the right taxes. I want to go beyond that,” Cayetano responded. “I want to pay my P170,000 — and you won’t accept it?”
The senator went on to paint a vision of how wealthy businessmen might wish to pay for themselves and their families.
“What if they’re feeling generous, and they have one or two kasambahay and they want to pay for it?” he added.
Even overseas Filipino workers might contribute smaller amounts over time — a few hundred dollars here and there, he imagined.
And if you’re wondering where this sudden wave of generosity might come from, Cayetano made an appeal to divine intervention.

“If we pray but we do not act, the Bible says faith without action is dead. So we cannot keep praying for a miracle without doing anything to open the door for that miracle,” he said, hoping the government would pave the way for a little divine intervention and a flood of donations.

blocks.caption: Escudero calls out fire effect in Sara Duterte trial livestream

blocks.text: As unusual as the proposal sounds, Cayetano does reference a historical example.

During the 1997 Asian financial crisis, millions of South Koreans famously gathered their gold jewelry to help their country overcome a severe foreign currency shortage. Around 3.51 million citizens contributed some 227 metric tons of gold, either donated or sold, to raise much-needed dollars.
Of course, South Korea’s campaign was about easing a foreign currency crisis, rather than paying off government debt, and it was only one part of the country’s economic recovery.
“Why can’t it happen to us?” Cayetano asked.
“If our debt were low and our debt payments were small, I wouldn’t be proposing that we bayanihan our way out,” he added in Filipino.

Of course, the good senator’s proposal, however well-intentioned, takes a few liberties with how national debt actually works. But let’s indulge the thought experiment. Can Filipinos really bayanihan their way out of debt?

Philippine government debt had reached P19.66 trillion as of end-September and is projected to reach P21.48 trillion by end-2027. Even if one million generous Filipinos each contributed P170,000, that would raise P170 billion, less than 1% of the projected debt.
Interest payments alone are programmed to reach P1.114 trillion next year, eating up more than 15% of the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget.
Economists previously told Rappler that the country’s debt remains manageable for now, although its rising size and cost are becoming concerning, especially as economic growth slows.

And besides, even Cayetano himself acknowledged what is perhaps the bigger problem with his proposal. Why would Filipinos voluntarily give the government more money when so many already distrust how it spends what they pay in taxes?
“The sentiment now is that everyone in government is a thief, that you’re all thieves, that we’re all thieves, and that no one wants to donate,” he said in a mix of English and Filipino.

And with a sitting vice president on trial for unexplained wealth, a proposed national budget riddled with red flags — roads whose coordinates lead straight into the sea and an overabundance of multi-purpose buildings — who exactly would be lining up to fork over another P170,000? – Rappler.com
